independent_findings.finding: Finite-number rejection is necessary but not sufficient for deterministic owner-visible numeric projection. The current adapter preserves signed negative zero as -0.0, accepts any finite magnitude up to float range, and relies on float() normalization whose overflow path for very large integers is not normalized to the module's bounded ValueError contract. These do not grant authority, but can create representation/replay or presentation inconsistencies across downstream consumers.
bounded_repair: Introduce a versioned DASHBOARD_NUMERIC_PROJECTION_POLICY; all magnitude/precision limits remain TEST_REQUIRED until calibrated.
Canonicalize -0.0 to +0.0 before projection if numeric hashes/equality are expected downstream.
Define an explicit finite magnitude envelope for owner-visible metrics or else emit a bounded OUT_OF_DISPLAY_RANGE status/reference instead of raw extreme values; the numeric bound is TEST_REQUIRED.
Catch float normalization OverflowError/TypeError and fail closed with a stable dashboard error code rather than runtime-dependent exception shape.
Keep Decimal/arbitrary numeric objects rejected unless a future version defines deterministic decimal canonicalization.
